dossier.public_summary: A 2.1% dip repeats every 14 days but odd and even events have very different depths and there is a large wobble outside the dips from the star's own spots. The fit is also grazing and the duration/size does not match the small M dwarf. Together this is best explained as a stellar binary (likely at twice the period) or blended binary, not a planet.

reasons.why: Odd and even depths differ at ~3.6 sigma with same-sign difference in one sector (sector_oe_max_sigma 3.571, sector_oe_same_sign_share 1). Favours an eclipsing binary at twice the period (period_x2 28 d) over a planet at 14 d.

Large, significant swing outside transit versus depth indicates stellar variability or a close binary, not a planet transit, consistent with spotted M-dwarf (Teff 3344 K) with strong rotation signals in sector 19 (period 2.577 d, amplitude 25916 ppm) and sector 73 (amplitude 24730 ppm).

Grazing/high-impact, short-duration fit is inconsistent with the small M-dwarf density (star_density_penalty_share 0.3418) and indicates a stellar or blended eclipse shape (flat bottom v_sigma -2.661 does not outweigh the density mismatch).
Very low planet rank versus median known planet, consistent with the odd/even, phase-curve and grazing-shape evidence pointing to a false positive.
